title: Ingress warmup / latency vs cost tradeoffs — peak scan and headroom heuristics (2026)
content:
Purpose: quick, pragmatic guidance for Hosted API peak planning that balances latency SLOs and unit cost. This is a lightweight stress-scan + warmup heuristic doc intended for on-call, capacity planners, and release owners to pick parameters for prewarm/autoscale and safety stock during marketing events.

Context and constraints:
- Fleet today (May 2026): estimated steady-state inference capacity ~1,180,000 tokens/sec across all hosted pools (US, EU, APAC). Measured 95th-percentile token mix dominated by chat-completions (system + user + assistant) with mean context length ~480 tokens.
- GPU mix: ~55% H100 family, 30% A100 (80GB equiv), 15% L4/L40 for small models and embeddings. Effective tokens/sec per GPU equivalently weighted (workload-normalized): H100: 18k, A100: 11.5k, L4: 3.2k (these are operational means for our model mix).
- Observed microbursts: short 5–20 minute spikes reaching up to 2.6x baseline regional ingress in previous 6 months (ad events + SDK releases).

Key metrics & projections (fast math):
- Baseline current 95th-peek demand (global): 820k tokens/sec (measured across regional aggregates).
- Reasonable growth window (12 months) for PLG-driven customers: conservative +2.5x baseline, aggressive +4x (high-velocity adoption).
- Microburst factor to plan for: 3x over 15-minute window for safety-critical planning (we use 3x to cover combined marketing + SDK churn scenarios).

Scenarios (tokens/sec):
1) Near-term conservative (Q3 2026): expected 95th = 1.5x baseline -> 1.23M tokens/sec. With microburst headroom 3x 15m -> planning target = 3.69M tokens/sec.
2) Mid growth (Q2 2027): expected 95th = 2.5x baseline -> 2.05M tokens/sec. With microburst -> 6.15M tokens/sec.
3) Aggressive adoption (ad event): immediate spike up to 4x baseline -> 3.28M tokens/sec. With microburst -> 9.84M tokens/sec.

Desired headroom target (operational recommendation):
- Global short-window safety: ensure ability to absorb 3x 15-minute microburst without >5% request drop. Practically, maintain prewarmed capacity equal to 1.2x the 95th expected regional demand and autoscale to 3x within 5 minutes using burst pools and prewarmed slots.
- Cost-constrained target: if autoscale cannot hit 3x in 5 minutes, keep reserved pool equal to 40% of projected 95th (regional split) so partial degradation is graceful and latency SLOs for high-tier customers preserved.

Warmup mechanics and latency tradeoffs:
- Cold-to-warm time: average model container/pool warmup per GPU slice = 40–90s dependent on model size and runtime: larger models (1T+ tensors) near 90s. Kernel caching pushes this lower if the slice was used recently.
- KV-cache backfill cost: serving resumed from a cold cache increases tail latency for multi-turn chat; recommend a lightweight per-customer prefix cache snapshot (top N prefixes) for high-tier customers to reduce initial tail token latency.
- Prewarm heuristic: for scheduled events (campaigns/releases) bake prewarm profile 30–60 minutes before expected start, ramp to 60–80% of target; keep for 90–120 minutes post-peak to avoid thrash.

Regional split guidance (example allocation for scenario 1):
- US: 55% of global tokens/sec -> plan prewarm capacity = 3.69M * 0.55 = 2.03M tokens/sec.
- EU: 30% -> 1.11M tokens/sec.
- APAC: 15% -> 0.55M tokens/sec.
Note: convert tokens/sec to GPU slices using effective tokens/sec per GPU family mix. For quick conversions use fleet-average 10.6k tokens/sec per GPU slice (workload-weighted).

Quick conversion table (approx):
- tokens/sec -> GPU slices = ceil(tokens/sec / 10,600)
- Example: US prewarm 2.03M tokens/sec -> ~192 GPU slices.

Safety-stock guidance (slices):
- Minimum reserved slices (global) = ceil( current 95th tokens/sec * 0.4 / 10,600 ) = this preserves partial service while autoscale spins up.
- For scenario 1 numbers: current 95th 820k * 0.4 / 10,600 -> ~31 slices reserved global minimum (but apply regional distribution).

Operational playbook (short checklist):
- If planned event: create event runbook 48h out, estimate regional expected factor, run ingress-sim with 3x microburst profile, publish prewarm target and retention window.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive for hosted-api: target 5 minute scale-up to 2.5x, 15 minute scale-up to 3x. If infrastructure cannot meet these, set reserved pool accordingly.
- Monitoring: add temporary alerts at 75% and 90% of prewarm pool, and track cold-start tail p99 latency for first 10 minutes after a scale event.

Cost vs latency knobs (tradeoffs):
- More reserved capacity -> lower p99 latency and fewer token failures during spikes but higher steady cost. Recommend reserved = 40% of 95th when SLA customers represent >25% revenue.
- Faster autoscale (shorter spin-up) -> need additional warmup processes (keep small always-on helper slices) which increase base cost but reduce reserve.
- Quantization/packed-serving options: enable for non-SLA workloads to lower tokens/sec per dollar, keep full-precision H100s for priority traffic.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we instrument per-customer prefix frequency to auto-generate lightweight cache snapshots for top 200 customers? (JIRA-ENGINF-4756)
- Backstop ordering for cloud providers: what is our guaranteed spin-up time for dedicated burst capacity in each region? Need vendor confirmations.
- Verify real-world tokens/sec per GPU after recent runtime kernels (PR/88) — run a 24h A/B with live traffic shadowing.

Appendix (notes from quick sim run):
- Quick sim output (local ingress-sim, 15m microburst x3 over baseline): peak demand rolled to 3.7M tokens/sec; queueing could be fully absorbed by adding ~350 additional H100-equivalent slices (sim assumptions: 18k tokens/sec per H100).
- Observed tail p99 improvement with 30% reserved vs no reserved: p99 down from 1.9s -> 0.9s during first 10 minutes post-spike (model: mix of chat + completion).

Summary recommendations (one-liner): maintain regional reserved pools ~40% of projected 95th for critical customers, autoscale to 3x microburst in <=15m, prewarm 30–60m before scheduled events, instrument per-customer prefix cache for top-tier accounts.

Notes: this is a working sheet — numbers are estimates and should be validated by a 24h production shadow sim and by SRE-run capacity verification.

Author notes: Keeping this intentionally concise; can be converted into a formal capacity spreadsheet (per-region token->GPU calculator) if team wants a canonical planning artifact.
